evidence:
host/store-write-host.lisp:819-824
  (let* ((w (fn-xw-sys (fn-hx-pwrite-zeros h offset count)))
         (w (if (fn-xw-okp w) (fn-xw-log-at "log-truncated") w))
         (w (if (fn-xw-okp w) (fn-xw-sys (fn-hx-fdatasync h)) w))
         ...)
    (if (not (fn-xw-okp w))
        (mv w store replay fn-octets-lg fn-arena)
Both earlier failure paths do `(prog2$ (fn-hx-close h) ...)` (lines 812 and 817). This one returns without closing h, and h is not yet in :log, so fn-xw-close cannot reach it either.
fix: Close h on this path too. Map an :os from the zero write or its barrier to fn-xw-indeterminate ("log tail truncation outcome is indeterminate"), as fn-xw-fence and fn-xw-commit-open-batch do for their writes.
reviewer: host/store-write-host.lisp:819-824: when the pwrite-zeros or fdatasync fails, the code returns w without (fn-hx-close h), unlike the paths at 812 and 817, and h is not yet in :log. The leak is real but harmless: `store ROOT recover` is a one-shot process, and the native fnn-log-recover (io.lisp:6705-6720) also leaves the fd open on these errors and reports them as an OS failure through fnn-os-fail. Reporting it as :os rather than :indeterminate loses nothing. The open fails, nothing else is mutated, and re-running recover re-zeroes the same tail [F, extent), which is idempotent and already dropped or quarantined. So the 'misclassified half-zeroed segment' part of the claim is not a real hazard.
scenario: During `store ROOT recover`, pwrite of the zeroed tail fails partway (ENOSPC or EIO) or the fdatasync fails. The O_RDWR descriptor on the active segment stays open, and fn-xw-recover passes the result up as `(:os ...)`. The segment's tail has been partly overwritten with unknown durability, but the outcome reaches the caller as an ordinary OS failure, not as :indeterminate like the other post-mutation failures in this file.
title: fn-xw-log-recover leaks the read-write segment handle when the tail zeroing or its barrier fails, and reports the half-zeroed segment as a plain OS error
